comment: TypeScript `this` and `object` used as types, like `clone(): this` or `a: object`. The builtin grammar gives them the same `support.type.builtin` scope as the literal types `true`, `false`, `null` and `undefined`, so they would be highlighted as constants. They are type keywords, same as `string` or `any`, so this rule scopes them as `support.type.primitive`. The scope has no language suffix, since the same rule is injected into TS and TSX.

patterns.comment: Not property or parameter names (`object: T`, `this?: T`, `m(): T`), `this is T` predicates, or `this.x`
patterns.name: support.type.primitive
